html:
The Berar Sultanate was one of the five Deccan sultanates, ruled by the Imad Shahi dynasty in the north east of today's Maharashtra from 1490 to 1574. Its capital was Ellichpur.

It was born when the Bahmani Sultanate broke apart. Its governor, Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk, a convert born to a Hindu family, declared himself independent in 1490. The other pieces became Ahmadnagar, Bijapur, Golconda and Bidar.

Berar was rich in cotton but squeezed between larger neighbours, and in 1574 Ahmadnagar annexed it. The Mughals took Berar in 1596. It later passed to the Nizams of Hyderabad, who assigned it to the British in 1853.
